instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Keep the newest posts of the forums I name (subreddits), with their titles, words, scores and comment counts, from a public archive of the site", and give it forums (Forums by name (a subreddit without r/): {forum: group}, or a list of names or { name, group }; group is your own word for who writes there, kept on each post).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:keep-forum-posts-from-a-public-archive and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: For each forum (a subreddit) asks the Arctic Shift public archive of Reddit (a third-party service, not the site itself) for its newest posts, a page of 100 at a time, each page older than the last, up to `pages` pages a forum (6 when left out), and keeps each post's id, link, title, words, score, comment count and time, with the forum and the group you name for it.
